# Community Support

`customer_support.model.community_support` · model · parent `—`

> Users answer each other in public, and the company curates rather than responds. This is the only branch in the tree with no owner and no clock by construction — not by neglect, by design. A question posted to a forum is assigned to nobody, breaches nothing when it is ignored, and simply sinks down the page. The characteristic failure is therefore not slowness, which announces itself, but silence, which does not: an unanswered thread produces no alert, no ageing metric and no unhappy customer in any system we own, because the unhappy customer left without telling us. . The second structural fact is that answer authority is unknown and answer permanence is total. A confident wrong answer from a well-regarded member looks identical to a correct one, is indexed within days, and will be the first thing the next thousand people with that problem read — for years, including after the product changed. Correction cost is asymmetric: fixing a wrong ticket costs one reply, fixing a wrong thread means editing a public record that other people have already linked to, and the community will read the edit as the company overruling its own members. . Third: the audience is not the asker. Most of the value accrues to people who search, read and leave without posting, so any measurement built on threads-answered or time-to-first-reply is measuring a rounding error of the actual benefit — and, worse, will justify staffing decisions that optimise for the visible tenth. . Fourth: the labour is volunteered, so it cannot be managed. The scarce resource is the goodwill of a dozen or so unpaid experts, and every mechanism a support org reaches for by reflex — targets, coverage rotas, quality scores, performance conversations — spends that goodwill faster than it improves anything. They can be recognised, informed and given early access. They cannot be assigned. . What an operator carries over wrongly from a queue: the idea that a paying customer in the forum is being served. Entitlement does not exist here, so a customer with a four-hour contractual response can post, wait three days, and get an answer from a stranger — and there is no mechanism in this branch that notices, because noticing requires the one capability the branch does not have. Lifting entitled customers out of the community and into the queue is a boundary that must be built deliberately at intake; it does not emerge.


## Characteristics

|  |  |
|---|---|
| requester | self-selected users, mostly unauthenticated or loosely identified, ranging from the most sophisticated power users in the base to people who found the thread from a search engine and never used the product |
| typical_resolution_hours | 72 |
| volume_shape | high thread volume with an extremely long tail of near-duplicates; readership outweighs participation by orders of magnitude and peaks long after the thread went quiet |
| staffing_model | a small moderation and curation team plus unpaid expert members; nobody is assigned to anything and answering is voluntary on both sides |
| coverage | whenever someone happens to be reading — which correlates with the community's own timezone concentration, not with ours |
| automation_level | high by side effect rather than by design — the archive deflects far more than the live threads resolve, and search is the real product |
| primary_channels | `community_forum`, `help_center`, `chat` |
| notes | The median time to resolution is a meaningless statistic in this branch and quoting it is a reliable sign the community is being run by someone from a queue. The distribution is bimodal: answered within an hour by someone who happened to be online, or never answered at all. There is no middle, so an average sits in a region where no thread actually lives.  |

## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.knowledge_article`

Requires `accuracy_state`, `last_verified_at`, `findability`, `audience`


> A high-ranking thread is a knowledge article that nobody owns, nobody verified and nobody will retire. The canonical object assumes an owner and a verification date; here both are legitimately absent, and the object must be able to say "unowned" rather than default to someone. `findability` outranks accuracy in practice — a correct answer that does not surface in search has no effect on anything, and an incorrect one that does is the branch's largest liability.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.requester`

Requires `technical_fluency`, `is_affected_user`


> Almost every identity attribute the canonical object carries is unavailable here: no account, no plan, no role, frequently not even a verified email. What remains is what can be read from the post itself — how fluent they are and whether the problem is actually theirs. Inferring anything more from a forum handle is invention, and the confidence on any such read should reflect that.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.customer_sentiment`

Requires `public_exposure`, `expression_style`


> Sentiment expressed in public behaves differently from sentiment in a ticket: it is performed for an audience, it recruits agreement, and a thread of eleven people saying "same here" is one problem and eleven relationships. `public_exposure` is the attribute that separates a complaint from an incident in this branch.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.escalation`

Requires `origin`, `reason`


> The only escalation that exists here is outward: from a thread into a real ticket, an incident, or engineering. There is no receiving owner inside the community to name, so an escalation that is not accepted by a named person on the company side has not happened — it is a moderator hoping somebody reads the channel.

## Metadata

owner **Customer Support** · updated 2026-08-08 · review **unreviewed** · confidence **experimental**


> This branch is the clearest case in the domain for pending signals over borrowed ones. The triggers that matter — a thread with no reply, a thread whose accepted answer is now wrong, a zero-result search, an entitled customer posting in public — have no analogue in the shipped substrate, and the nearest available type (unanswered_email) is about a message we owe a reply to, which is exactly the relationship a forum does not have.
